claim_checks.claim: Collision resolution — its job: find another place for colliding keys, by chaining or open addressing
claim_checks.page_says: There are many collision resolution schemes, but they may be divided into open addressing, chaining, and keeping one special overflow area.
claim_checks.note: The page divides schemes into three classes; the claim names only two and drops 'keeping one special overflow area'. The page also does not describe resolution as 'find another place for colliding keys' (chaining keeps them at the same position).

claim_checks.claim: Map to a position: keys are mapped to array positions by the hash function; more than one key mapping to the same position is a collision
claim_checks.page_says: A dictionary in which keys are mapped to array positions by hash functions. Having the keys of more than one item map to the same position is called a collision.

claim_checks.claim: Resolve collisions: schemes divide into chaining and open addressing
claim_checks.page_says: There are many collision resolution schemes, but they may be divided into open addressing, chaining, and keeping one special overflow area.
claim_checks.note: The claim states a two-way division; the cited page gives a three-way one, so the claim gives a different classification than its source.

claim_checks.claim: CPython's dict uses open addressing — "Open addressing is preferred over chaining since the link overhead for chaining would be substantial" — with the initial probe at hash mod table size
claim_checks.page_says: not found (searched: open addressing, chaining, link overhead, substantial, preferred). The page has: "in a table of size 2**i, taking the low-order i bits as the initial table index is extremely fast"
claim_checks.note: The initial-index part is supported (low-order i bits of the hash in a table of size 2**i equals hash mod table size), and the page describes probing other indices ('visit table indices via this recurrence'). But the quoted sentence is not in the saved text, and the page never uses the words 'open addressing'. The saved render is GitHub's truncated view of the file, so the quote may exist past the cut; it is not in what was saved.

claim_checks.claim: Java's HashMap resizes (roughly doubling buckets) when entries exceed capacity × load factor; "the default load factor (.75) offers a good tradeoff between time and space costs"
claim_checks.page_says: exceeds the product of the load factor and the current capacity ... approximately twice the number of buckets ... the default load factor (.75) offers a good tradeoff
claim_checks.note: The quoted sentence is verbatim on the page; the resize threshold and doubling match.

claim_checks.claim: Cost: constant-time get and put "assuming the hash function disperses the elements properly among the buckets"
claim_checks.page_says: This implementation provides constant-time performance for the basic operations (get and put), assuming the hash function disperses the elements properly among the buckets.

claim_checks.claim: Why the Bad class is quadratic: inserting the k-th key compares it with all k − 1 earlier keys ... With Good, each insert lands on its own slot almost always, so the total is linear
claim_checks.page_says: not checkable: cites only the local artifact linux/lab-setup.md, which has no saved text
claim_checks.note: The arithmetic (n²/2, about 2 million comparisons at 2,000 keys) is derived, not measured; the 4,000-key figure is a prediction with no run behind it.

claim_checks.claim: The same mechanism is a denial-of-service risk when attackers choose keys (e.g. request parameters) that collide; language runtimes therefore randomize string hashing per process
claim_checks.page_says: protection against a denial-of-service caused by carefully chosen inputs ... a random value is used to seed the hashes of str and bytes objects ... Specifying the value 0 will disable hash randomization.
claim_checks.note: The page covers Python only; the claim widens it to 'language runtimes'. It also drops the condition that randomization is the default and is fixed or disabled when PYTHONHASHSEED is set to an integer. 'request parameters' is not on the page. The DoS purpose and per-process constancy are supported.

violations.evidence: C2 (contradicted): the actor list says collision resolution works 'by chaining or open addressing'; [^1] divides schemes into open addressing, chaining, and keeping one special overflow area, and does not say resolution means finding another place.
C4 (contradicted): step 2 says 'schemes divide into chaining and open addressing'; [^1] gives a three-way division that includes keeping one special overflow area.

C5 (unsupported): the quoted sentence 'Open addressing is preferred over chaining since the link overhead for chaining would be substantial' is not in the saved text of [^2], which is GitHub's truncated render of dictobject.c; the words 'open addressing' and 'chaining' do not appear.

C9 (overstates): 'language runtimes therefore randomize string hashing per process' widens a Python-only page [^5] to all runtimes and drops the PYTHONHASHSEED condition (an integer seed fixes the hash, 0 disables randomization); 'request parameters' is not on the page.

Role 4 holds no run of its own: the real run (code and timings) sits in ## Mental model, this section explains it with derived arithmetic and a predicted 4,000-key cost, and its second paragraph (hash-flooding DoS) is a failure mode that belongs in role 6.
